data.claim: a hand gate record carries chunk_findings from the failed review, so triage_counts counts them untriaged on the later passed record
data.falsifier: status shows 0 untriaged after failed review then hand pass
data.mechanism: handlers/gates.py inherits chunk_findings (B754cfb0c96); triage_counts ignores the outcome
data.probe: repro test: review (3 findings) then gate record passed, read status triage line
data.probe_output: unfixed: '3 finding(s): 0 refuted, 0 confirmed, 3 untriaged' next to [x]; the [!] mark did not reproduce (latest outcome folds correctly)
data.question: Why does gate status count untriaged findings after a later pass?

chunk_findings.detail: `evidence.setdefault("findings_carried", True)` is executed whenever the prior record has `chunk_findings`, i.e. unconditionally inside that block — it is not tied to whether the carry actually happened. The line above (`evidence.setdefault("chunk_findings", prior["chunk_findings"])`) deliberately does nothing when the new record's evidence already supplies its own `chunk_findings`, yet `findings_carried` is still set to `True`. Then in `ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py`, `triage_counts` computes `left` from those (new, never-carried) digests and `_passed_over_carried(rec)` returns `True`, so `untriaged` is forced to 0 and the status prints `N settled by the later pass` instead of `N untriaged`. Concrete input: prior gate evidence `{"chunk_findings": [A, B, C]}`; a later hand `gate passed` whose evidence is `{"chunk_findings": [D, E]}` and has no `review_kind` → `D`/`E` are reported as settled by the pass (status hides that they are untriaged, and the "about to follow" note is suppressed), reintroducing exactly the class of bug (untriaged findings not visible) that this change is meant to fix. The marker should only be set when the copy from `prior` actually occurred.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/handlers/gates.py:41

chunk_findings.detail: Bug B29667ba4b4 has two expected behaviours: (1) the gate status reflects the latest recorded outcome, and (2) `ddflow review triage ITEM` lists the findings with their ids instead of only printing "say which: --refuted or --confirmed". This regression file only exercises (1). The single call into the triage path, `api.triage(repo, "T1", gate="critic", finding=1, verdict="confirmed", probe="saw it")`, discards the returned data and is followed only by `assert "2 untriaged" in _status_line(repo)`, i.e. it checks the *status count*, never the triage output. So if the listing half of the fix regressed back to the old wording (the exact symptom in the repro: "say which: --refuted or --confirmed" with no finding ids), every test in this file still passes, and the bug can be reopened unnoticed. A regression test intended to close this bug should assert on the triage result / CLI output that the findings (with ids) are printed; that assertion is absent, so half of the bug is unprotected. [D-rules-hierarchy]
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_status_latest_round.py:49 (`test_a_still_failed_round_keeps_its_untriaged_count` / missing triage-listing assertion)

chunk_findings.detail: Bug B29667ba4b4 has two expected behaviours: (1) `gate status` reflects the latest recorded outcome, and (2) `ddflow review triage ITEM` lists the findings with their ids so the untriaged ones can be seen. The diff only rewrites the `bad(...)` string — the branch still returns a single message and never emits the findings/numbers. Concretely, given an item whose critic gate carries findings and was later passed (`findings_carried` set by the new `gates.py` code), invoking `ddflow review triage ITEM` with no `--refuted`/`--confirmed` still returns only "say which: --refuted (...) or --confirmed (`ddflow review show {item}` lists the findings with their numbers)" — the output contains no finding ids, so behaviour (2) is still not met by the triage path; the change merely redirects the user to a different command. This is the earlier review's finding 2, and the fix (a message rewrite plus the `settled_by_pass` zeroing in `outcomes.py`) does not answer it: neither a listing nor a test asserting one appears in the change, and the pointer text does not itself list the carried finding numbers the user must triage. (The earlier finding 1 is answered: `findings_carried` is now set only inside `if "chunk_findings" not in evidence:`, i.e. exactly when the carry occurs, so it is no longer set when the new record supplies its own `chunk_findings`.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/review.py:272 (`triage`, the `verdict not in ("refuted", "confirmed")` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: Bug B29667ba4b4 states two expected behaviours: (1) gate status reflects the latest recorded outcome, and (2) `ddflow review triage ITEM` must *list the findings with their ids* instead of only saying "say which: --refuted or --confirmed". The new triage assertion only checks `"ddflow review show T1" in out.reason`, i.e. that the message points the user at a different command. It never asserts that a single finding id (or the findings at all) appears in the triage output, and it inspects nothing else on the returned object. So an implementation that still prints essentially "say which: --refuted or --confirmed; see `ddflow review show T1`" — leaving the untriaged findings invisible in the triage call itself — passes this test, and the second half of the bug stays unverified. Concretely, with `_setup(repo, tmp_path, 2)` there are findings 1 and 2; the call `api.triage(repo, "T1", gate="critic", finding=1, verdict="", probe="")` can return a reason of the form `"say which: --refuted or --confirmed (see ddflow review show T1)"`, and this regression file still goes green even though the user cannot see from the triage output which findings are untriaged — the exact symptom the bug reports. The previous finding #2 therefore still holds; the added pointer assertion does not answer it because it tests that a hint string is present, not that the findings with their ids are listed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_status_latest_round.py:79 (`test_triage_without_a_verdict_points_at_the_findings`)

chunk_findings.detail: A hand gate record whose outcome is `passed` and which merely *inherits* findings sets `findings_carried`, and `triage_counts` then forces `untriaged = 0` for **every** inherited finding, without any check that the pass actually resolved them. Concrete input: a review records 4 findings on the gate (`chunk_findings`, none triaged); the operator then records a hand record `ddflow gate passed ITEM --gate critic --evidence "3 fixed, 1 deferred"` (or even with no evidence at all). In `gates.py` the handler copies all 4 findings onto the pass and stamps `findings_carried=True`; back in `triage_counts`, `left` is 4 and `_passed_over_carried(rec)` is True, so it returns `{findings: 4, untriaged: 0, settled_by_pass: 4}`, and `untriaged_note` returns `""` because `counts.get("settled_by_pass")` is truthy. `ddflow gate status` therefore prints `4 finding(s): 0 refuted, 0 confirmed, 0 untriaged, 4 settled by the later pass` and drops the `next = critic` pointer, even though the pass's own evidence only accounts for 3 of the 4 findings (the repro's pass says "all 3 findings confirmed and fixed" against a status that reports "4 finding(s)"). The fourth, never-triaged finding is silently presented as settled, and because the suppression is keyed on a boolean flag rather than on the pass's recorded disposition, nothing distinguishes a pass that resolved the findings from one that deferred them.
